subject: Post-call: perf SLOs, streaming constraints & benchmark handoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Luke Tanner <ltanner@canopyai.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: perf SLOs, streaming constraints & benchmark handoff

Luke — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a reproducible run on our side: 

Recap / SLO targets you mentioned:
- p95 end-to-end generation latency target: <= 200ms for short responses (~32 tokens)
- p99 latency budget: <= 400ms (hard cap)
- Sustained throughput target: 120 qps for single-region traffic
- Concurrency expectation: 80 concurrent sessions (streaming enabled)
- Streaming requirements: token-level streaming with ~64-token chunk cadence, low-jitter delivery

What we need from you to proceed with a benchmark handoff:
1) Representative prompt set + any private fields removed (you can drop into the Drive link below).
2) Clarification on typical sequence length distribution (percentiles for 16/32/64/128 token lengths).
3) Any firewall/ingress constraints for our dedicated test pods (IP allowlist window).
4) Preferred test window (we usually run 2-hour windows M-F 07:00–20:00 PT).

Proposed next steps:
- You share prompt set and sequence-length histogram (action: Canopy)
- Our infra team (Nikhil, Priyom) will draft a benchmark harness configuration + measurement spec (action: Redwood)
- Schedule a 1-hr run verification + results sync next week

I attached a short instruction doc that outlines our typical eval harness and what we measure (tail latencies, token throughput, cold vs warm KV-cache). If you want us to run in your VPC/Private deployment, note that we'll need an allowlist and service account prior to test.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Luke Tanner <ltanner@canopyai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Canopy AI - Procurement <procurement@canopyai.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf SLOs, streaming constraints & benchmark handoff

Thanks Marissa — great recap. Confirming the targets are accurate for our current product lane. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sequence lengths: 12 tokens (30%), 32 tokens (45%), 80 tokens (20%), >150 tokens (5%). We will upload a sanitized prompt set to your Drive link by EOD Monday.
- Streaming: we need per-chunk delivery latency to be consistent; jitter above ~75ms causes a poor UX for our client streaming.
- Warm vs cold: most production traffic hits warm KV-cache for user sessions; we can provide a set of long-running session traces to simulate cache state if that helps.
- Reproducibility: please define how you compute p95/p99 (server-side token emit vs end-to-end TCP ack). We prefer end-to-end seen-by-client timings.

Procurement looped in for the benchmark engagement form. We'll also need a short non-disclosure addendum for the prompt set (we're OK with sanitized test data but prefer a narrow NDA clause).

Luke
Director of AI Ops, Canopy AI
ltanner@canopyai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Canopy benchmark configuration + measurement defs

Team — Canopy confirmed sequence distribution and streaming jitter requirements. Draft measurement plan below; please review and edit before we send to Luke.

Measurement definitions (proposal):
- Request definition: full HTTP request -> last token delivered. For streaming, measure at two points: (A) server emit timestamp per chunk, (B) client-received timestamp (simulated by harness). We will report both; primary SLO will follow client-seen end-to-end timings.
- Latency metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 end-to-end for full response; per-chunk median and p95 jitter for streaming chunks.
- Throughput: sustained successful responses per second over 10-minute sliding windows; include token throughput (tokens/sec).
- Concurrency: measured as active sessions (connections with streaming open).
- Cold vs Warm: run two passes — cold (fresh runtime, no KV cache) and warm (pre-warmed with 1k representative sessions). Report deltas.
- Reproducibility: seed all RNGs, pin model version & quantization profile, capture hardware topology (GPU model + driver), and commit harness run config to the runner repo.

Test harness notes: use redwood-eval-runner v1.2 (link below) in dockerized mode. We will provide a runner config that maps Canopy prompt set to our concurrency/arrival profile. Warmup time will be 20 minutes, then 60-minute measured window.

Risks / constraints: network variance for cross-region traffic — recommend running in Canopy's preferred region to reduce noise. Also ensure chunk size alignment: they asked for ~64-token chunk cadence; we'll simulate that by splitting responses into 64-token flushes.

Can you take the measurement defs and produce a short email back to Canopy? I'll attach the harness instructions and the sample result schema.

-Marissa
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Canopy benchmark configuration + measurement defs

SGTM. A few concretes I'm adding to the harness doc before we share: 

- Runner command (example): 
  docker run --rm 
    -e RUN_MODE=measure 
    -e PROMPT_SET=/data/canopy_promptset_v1.json 
    -e CONCURRENCY=80 
    -e TARGET_QPS=120 
    redwood/eval-runner:v1.2 
  # Will emit JSONL of per-request events with server_emit_ts and client_seen_ts

- We'll include a reproducibility header in run outputs: git_sha, docker_image, GPU model, kernel, quant_profile, seed.
- KV-cache warmup: replay 1k session traces at 2x real-time rate to populate caches, wait 5 minutes stabilization, then start measured window.
- Streaming simulation: harness will open persistent HTTP/2 connections and simulate a client read loop with controllable network jitter (we can throttle to match Canopy's allowed jitter envelope).

I'm attaching the updated harness instructions PDF and a tiny sample results CSV. Once Marissa gives the go, I'll push the runner config to a branch and share a reproducible command.

-Nikhil
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Scheduling benchmark window + promptset share

Luke — looping back with the artifacts and a proposed slot. 

Artifacts shared:
- Drive: sanitized prompt set (canopy_promptset_v1.json) — access granted to ltanner@canopyai.com
- Harness instructions: redwood_eval_harness_instructions.pdf (attached)

Proposed test window: Thursday, May 7th 14:00–16:00 PT (2-hour window). Plan: 20m warmup, 1h measured run, 40m buffer for repeat or diagnostics. Please confirm whether that works for your SREs.

Data handling: prompts will be stored in an ephemeral bucket for the run and destroyed after result verification. We will not persist any user PII; please confirm sanitized set. Also, for the NDA addendum, procurement — can you confirm a point of contact so we can route the addendum?

Next steps on confirmation:
- Luke confirms test window + procurement contact
- We run the harness and share raw JSONL + aggregated metrics + replay scripts

Thanks — Priyom

Luke
